messages:
anna_support: FYI customer Nebula Labs (acct neb-3321) reports their Mar 12-13 invoice shows 0 reserved GPU hours but Console -> Dedicated Pool 'pool-nyc-prod-3' shows 14.5h consumed. They didn't receive SLA credits. Ticket #9876

raj_billing: can you drop the exact invoice line + pool id? Did they have burst enabled? :thinking:

anna_support: invoice snippet pasted in ticket: \"lineitem: dedicated_reserved_hours: 0.00\". Pool id: pool-nyc-prod-3. Burst config: enabled, burst_balance: 50h. Customer notes short spikes (spiky traffic) but token burn low (~1.2M tokens). They think GPU hours were consumed but never attributed for billing.

billing-bot: metering export ready for neb-3321: /exports/neb-3321/2026-03-12_13-metering.csv

lee_engineer: assigned to investigate. Quick hypothesis: attribution layer is dropping billing_pool_id on some metering events (agent label mismatch). I'll inspect the pool attribution pipeline (pool_attribution.py).

maria_cs: customer asked if we can issue a temporary credit while we investigate. Suggest small goodwill credit until we reconcile.

raj_billing: did a quick reconciliation: Console shows reserved_pool hours: 14.5h; metering export lists burst_hours: 12.2h; invoice shows 0 reserved and 0 burst line items for that interval. Looks like billing pipeline job failed to materialize line items for that range.

ops_sre: pulled ingestion logs for 2026-03-12T03:00-04:00Z. Found multiple metering events missing the mapping field. Sample event:
```
2026-03-12T03:11:22Z metering_event { "host": "gpu-43.nyc", "pool": "pool-nyc-prod-3", "reserved_hours": 1.0, "billing_pool_id": null, "job_id": "srv-xy" }
```
That null billing_pool_id will cause attribution to drop or assign to fallback, so billing job doesn't create reserved hour line. There's also a deploy at ~02:58 that touched agent labels.

lee_engineer: repro steps to validate locally:
1) python scripts/fetch_metering.py --org neb-3321 --start 2026-03-12 --end 2026-03-13 --pool pool-nyc-prod-3 --out events.json
2) python tools/pool_attribution.py --input events.json --map config/pool_map.yaml --out attributed.json
Expected: events[].billing_pool_id == "pool-nyc-prod-3"
Observed: ~40% of events have billing_pool_id == null

raj_billing: remediation plan:
- backfill billing_pool_id in the ingestion DB using host->pool mapping for 2026-03-12 03:00-04:00
- rerun billing pipeline for that range (recompute line items)
- issue provisional SLA credit to Nebula while backfill runs (propose 5% of disputed lines)
I'll prepare the job and PR to trigger rerun.

maria_cs: customer agreed to provisional credit while we investigate. They want ETA.

lee_engineer: ETA for backfill + rerun ~ 6 hours assuming no schema surprises. Will update if blocked. Also adding checks to attribution to fail loudly if billing_pool_id null rate > 1%.

anna_support: added notes to ticket #9876 and informed Nebula that we're working it, thanks. :thumbsup:

ops_sre: follow-up: found the 02:58 UTC deploy changed label key from \"billing_pool\" -> \"billing_pool_id\" in the new agent, but the agent rollout was partial and older processes still emit the old key. Some ingestion consumers only read the old key -> mapping mismatch. Root cause: inconsistent label key across agent versions.

raj_billing: kicking off backfill job now. Will attach run id. Plan: backfill ingestion table -> update billing_pool_id where null using host->pool map -> trigger billing-run for 2026-03-12T03:00-04:00.

billing-bot: billing_run_started { "run_id": "br-20260312-1801", "range": "2026-03-12T03:00:00Z/2026-03-12T04:00:00Z" }

lee_engineer: once backfill done, validate token->gpu correlation. Low token count with high GPU hours often indicates idle kernels or warmup overhead. Add post-run checks: kv_cache_hit_rate, active_seq_distribution, and per-host uptime to avoid double-charging idle time.

anna_support: perfect. I'll update Nebula with ETA and provisional credit details. Keep me posted here and in the ticket.
